clue.text: Exactly where does the rent go?

definitions.meaning: precisely, following instructions word for word
a tenant's rent is paid to the landlord, the one who lets the property

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: someone who lets a flat is a 'letter', so the rent goes to that person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something precisely as instructed is carrying it out with literal exactness; the second reading pays a landlord.

clue.text: Twitch at regular intervals?

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word Twitch, starting from its first

explanation.surface: A nervous jerk keeps recurring every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the first, third and fifth letters of Twitch gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes a nervous spasm that recurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary spasm of a muscle that tends to recur.

clue.text: Constellation reportedly in 'the shape of a doughnut

indicators.note: reportedly says the star group's name is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Taurus, the Bull, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star pattern is said to look like a ring doughnut.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TAURUS and TORUS are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a torus is the ring surface made by spinning a circle, like a ring doughnut.

clue.text: Being responsible for love I have found wearing

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they have found love tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like clothing but is the definition, in the sense of wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that wears away a surface gradually is abrasive or corrosive in action.

clue.text: Loriner wife gets most of premier residence and personal funds

parts.note: a former wife is an ex

indicators.note: most of says the final letter of the residence's name is dropped

parts.note: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence

explanation.surface: A divorcee claims nearly all of the Prime Minister's house as well as his money.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEQUERS is the official country house of the UK Prime Minister (the premier).
explanation.definitionFit: Exchequer is used humorously for a person's own finances or purse.

clue.text: Bill dropped by player, a lock

indicators.note: the bill's letters are taken away from the player's word

parts.note: an actress is a player on stage
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An actor is handed an invoice and a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair.

clue.text: Weakened by ill-health, fell.

definitions.meaning: to knock over or bring down, as a car does a pedestrian

explanation.definitionFit: Feeling exhausted is being in a poor state; to knock down a person is to strike them so they drop.

clue.text: Little'. fairy endlessly flitted around

indicators.note: around turns the shortened word back to front
endlessly drops the last letter of the word for flitted

parts.note: to flit is to move off quickly, to flee

explanation.surface: A small sprite darted to and fro without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small mischievous creatures of folklore, a kind of tiny sprite.

clue.text: Bound to catch corrupt cleric with no way out

indicators.note: to catch says the outer word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a dead end has no way out, so end

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters of cleric are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to trap a crooked priest who is cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges the cleric's letters; 'Bound' reads as a verb of obligation with 'to', but it means surrounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bound in is to be surrounded on all sides, ringed about.

clue.text: Waged war like Galahad' reported magazine

indicators.note: reported says the phrase before it is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: fought, in the manner of a knight such as Sir Galahad of the Round Table

explanation.surface: A periodical tells of Galahad's chivalrous battles.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent FOUGHT sounds like FORT, and KNIGHTLY like NIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A periodical issued every two weeks is called by its frequency of publication.

clue.text: Concern about technique needed for ornamental drawing

indicators.note: about says one word goes round the other

parts.note: concern means care
a player's touch is their technique or skill

explanation.surface: Skill is required for making a decorative sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is a decorative scroll-shaped frame or tablet, as on a map or Egyptian inscription.

clue.text: More pleasant French resort by river

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A town on the Riviera beside a river is more agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning agreeable.

clue.text: Right across road you'll find petrol

indicators.note: across says the fuel word spans either side of the road

parts.note: juice is slang for petrol or fuel
ST is short for street, a road

explanation.surface: Someone directs you over the road to a filling station.
explanation.definitionFit: Justice is what is right and fair.

clue.text: One must pull strings to operate this firework

definitions.text: One must pull strings to operate this
definitions.meaning: a jointed toy figure whose limbs jerk when its string is pulled
a cracker that jumps about as it explodes

explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a jerking puppet toy worked by string and a leaping cracker set off on bonfire night.

clue.text: Holds up kangaroo mother — finally managed to find pouch

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Holds up kangaroo mother — finally managed to find pouch'; no parse of these words builds SPORRAN, so the clue looks garbled by OCR and no source gives it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Holds up kangaroo mother — finally managed to find pouch

clue.text: Crop I planted in the middle of lots of paths

indicators.note: planted in the middle says the I goes inside the next piece

parts.note: a maze is a network of many paths

explanation.surface: A farmer sows a field at the centre of a labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or sweetcorn, is a cereal grown in fields.

clue.text: Secure against loss if my dinner not completely cooked

indicators.note: cooked says the letters are worked into a new order
not completely drops the last letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Someone wants insurance in case their meal is underdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' cuts DINNER to DINNE; 'cooked' rearranges IF MY DINNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To indemnify someone is to protect them against loss or damage by promising compensation.

clue.text: Standard group of workers employed by plant

parts.note: a trade union is a body of workers
a flag is an iris, a flowering plant

explanation.surface: A trade union is taken on by a factory as its usual practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is the iris. The UNION FLAG is the British national flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and this is the national one of the UK.

clue.text: Johnny-come-lately, one given one award after another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MM is the Military Medal, a British award
I again, the Roman numeral one
another award, a grant

explanation.surface: Someone receives one prize after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The pattern is one given an award, then one given another: I + MM, then I + GRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer who has just arrived from another country is a recent settler.

clue.text: Contemporary code broken by strange misbehaviour

parts.note: in means fashionable, contemporary

indicators.note: broken says the letters of code are rearranged

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A modern rulebook is flouted by some peculiar behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is a lack of propriety, improper behaviour.

clue.text: Take heed, around zero Celsius, climbing and turning on ice

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, says the letters are read from the bottom up
around says the watch word goes round the zero

parts.note: watch means take heed
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A skater is warned about freezing temperatures while doing a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' gives WATCOH, C is added, and 'climbing' reverses WATCOHC.
explanation.definitionFit: A choctaw is a figure-skating turn from one foot to the other.

clue.text: Inside part of French bathroom fitting

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Inside part of French bathroom fitting'; no parse of these words gives BIDET (it suggests BID + ET), so a word looks misread and no source gives the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Inside part of French bathroom fitting

clue.text: Wear something to cover face up with insect around

indicators.note: around says the insect goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the face covering is read from the bottom

parts.note: a veil covers the face

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a beekeeper's veil to keep the bees off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the veil backwards, as this is a down clue; 'Wear' means accept, as in 'I won't wear that excuse'.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British use, to wear a story is to accept or credit it.

clue.text: Soup I left, making mouth sore

parts.note: gumbo is a thick stew-like soup of the American South

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned their soup because their mouth hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboil is an abscess on the gum, a painful swelling inside the mouth.

clue.text: Some national assistance used for drink

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of state welfare money is spent on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'used for drink' as the definition; 'used for' is a link and only 'drink' can stand for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is an Indian yoghurt-based beverage.

clue.text: Gods largely ill-disposed

indicators.note: ill-disposed says the letters of largely are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Most deities are unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gods' are the cheap seats high up in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest balcony in a theatre is nicknamed the gods.

clue.text: Be discriminatory. — cut off first son

indicators.note: cut off first says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a sexist is discriminatory on grounds of gender

explanation.surface: A biased parent disinherits their eldest boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live or have being.

clue.text: Inclined to join a fight

parts.note: a tilt is a joust, a fight on horseback

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to join a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Atilt means tilted, leaning at an angle.

clue.text: Showing extreme desire to join Labour association

parts.note: to slave is to labour
a ring is a group or association, as of dealers

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to join a Labour Party branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but is the verb to toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavering, dribbling saliva, describes someone drooling with greed or longing.

clue.text: Doctor taking a break

indicators.note: taking says the doctor holds the A inside

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor goes on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an interval or pause.

clue.text: Island of vital importance

explanation.definitionFit: A cay is a low island and the same word spelt this way means crucial.

clue.text: Keep quiet in case operation is very fast with only brief. pauses

definitions.text: very fast with only brief. pauses

parts.note: whist is an old command for silence, hush
lest means in case

explanation.surface: A surgeon tells staff to hush in case the surgery is rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle-stop tour makes many quick stops of brief duration.
